items.serviceLabel: Ocean-Going Ad Hoc call America East Coast(OGEC)
items.teuSrc: Flexport Atlas, read 2026-09-02 12:00Z run (title confirmed IMO 9728916, body 14,354 TEU). NOT re-read this run - vessel particulars do not change between runs, so the figure is carried forward rather than re-scraped.

vsProforma.basis: Fastest direct proforma on the pair with an in-window September departure, taken across all three queryable sources: MSC/ZIM EMERALD SERVICE, ZIM CANADA 20E, Yantian 07 Sep to Savannah 05 Oct, 28d; Evergreen AUE, EVER MAX 1374-016E, 29d; Hapag US1, MAERSK LIRQUEN, 30d. OGEC TRITON runs 27d, so it is one day faster than the best proforma on this pair. Do not over-read that: on Yantian to New York the same voyage runs 31d against a fastest proforma of 26d (Evergreen SAX, OOCL DAFFODIL 006E, etd 10 Sep), a 5-day penalty. The honest summary is that TRITON is competitive to Savannah and clearly slower to New York, and should be priced as added capacity rather than as an expedited product. Note the movement since last run: last run put this pair at proforma 25d against OGEC 26d for delta +1, because MSC's fastest string then was ZIM MOUNT RAINIER 13E at 25d. That sailing is no longer in the September departure set and MSC's best has slipped to 28d, while OGEC slipped from 26d to 27d. Both numbers moved; the sign flipped for that reason, not because the product changed.

items.serviceLabel: Ocean-Going Ad Hoc call America East Coast(OGEC)
items.teuSrc: Flexport Atlas, read 2026-09-02 12:00Z run (title confirmed IMO 9595450, body 9,466 TEU). NOT re-read this run - carried forward.

vsProforma.basis: Fastest direct proforma on the pair with an in-window September departure, across all three queryable sources: Evergreen NUE2, COSCO SHIPPING ORCHID 035E, Pusan 16 Sep, 22d; MSC/ZIM EMPIRE, KOWLOON GE634E, Pusan 07 Sep, 23d; Hapag US2, COCHRANE, Pusan 11 Sep, 24d. OGEC EVER LASTING runs 28d from Pusan, so it is 6 days slower than the best proforma. The gap widens further up the coast: Shanghai to New York is 34d against a fastest proforma of 22d (Evergreen SAX, OOCL DAFFODIL 006E, etd 14 Sep), a 12-day penalty, and Ningbo to New York is 31d against 25d. This voyage is pure added capacity and carries no transit advantage on any pair. Last run's baseline used MSC EMPIRE at 23d and reported delta +5; the change to +6 comes from Evergreen's own NUE2 string being re-read this run and proving one day faster than MSC, not from any change to the OGEC schedule.

AA9 runs 38d Ningbo to New York, 13 days slower than the best proforma, and 42d Qingdao to Savannah. The five-day Balboa call (30 Sep to 05 Oct) is most of the difference and is characteristic of ad-hoc tonnage taking whatever canal slot it can get rather than a booked proforma window. Space relief only; there is no transit case for this sailing.

items.note: Single in-window sailing on a non-registry code, so it publishes as an extra loader under the n<=2 rule. Honest caveat: the carrier name string is "Asia America Service IX", which does NOT match the ad-hoc label regex. If a second and third AA9 sailing appear in later runs this is a NEW SERVICE, not an extra loader, and it should be promoted to the registry and dropped from items. The previous commit stamped updated as 2026-09-02T12:00:00Z while the real UTC clock at that commit was earlier the same day - the timestamp was the nominal schedule slot, not the actual run time. This run writes the true UTC instant, so updated moves backwards relative to the previous file. Any frontend that sorts or diffs on updated should be aware. Recommend future runs write real UTC.

Evergreen Yantian to New York 4wk returned SAX 4, CBX 4, AUE 4, OGEC 1 - only OGEC flagged. Evergreen Shanghai to New York returned SAX 3, NUE 4, NUE2 1, CBX 2, OGEC 1 - only OGEC flagged. Hapag Yantian to New York 8wk returned AA7 5 with isGemini false and US4 6 with isGemini true - nothing flagged, so the registry lookup and the isGemini trap are both behaving.

Logged, not published. Hapag Shanghai to New York showed US1 with n equal to 1 on a normally weekly lane, and Yantian to Savannah showed US1 with n equal to 2. Known registry code, so this is proforma thinning on the Gemini US1 string, not an extra loader.

Cai Mep resolves as VNVUT on the Hapag API, not VNCMT. VNCMT returned zero routes and would have been silently read as no service. VNVUT returned 13 direct routes (AA7 7, US4 6). The SCOPE line in the task file says VNCMT - it is wrong for Hapag and should be corrected there.

OGEC runs as a rolling programme - 0020 TRITON then 0021 EVER LASTING - so a 0022 was expected. None found on any of the eight Evergreen lanes this run. Cai Mep to New York returned SAX, CBX and AUE only, with no OGEC at all. Either 0022 has not been filed yet or it loads from a port not queried. Worth a targeted Kaohsiung and Hong Kong origin check next run.
